texts.title: A Vote for a Vote
texts.body: {senator.name} of {senator.house} has a motion before the Senate this session, and has come to count heads. {senator.He} wants your vote. {senator.He} does not offer money for it. {senator.He} offers a vote of {senator.his} own: give your word, and {senator.house} owes your house a vote. It votes for the next motion your house moves, whichever way it leans, unless that motion strikes at it. Your vote on {senator.his} motion is declared for it, and is still yours to change until the Senate sits; but a word given and not kept is written down, and {senator.house} takes no word of yours on a vote for eight years.

choices.give_your_word: Give your word, and take {senator.hers}. Vote for {senator.his} motion, or {senator.he} will remember it.
choices.name_a_price: Tell {senator.him} a vote costs more than a vote, and sell {senator.him} yours for {senator.his} motion.
choices.keep_your_vote: Tell them your vote is your own.

texts.title: A Bought Vote Called In
texts.body: {buyer.name} of {buyer.house} has another motion before the Senate. {buyer.He} paid for your vote once, and {buyer.he} has not forgotten it. {buyer.He} does not mean to pay again. A house that sells its vote once, {buyer.he} says, has told the chamber what it is, and {buyer.he} is sure you would not want the chamber reminded. The vote itself is cast in the chamber, as always, and {buyer.he} will be watching how you cast it.

choices.vote_as_they_ask: Say you will vote for it. Vote otherwise, and {buyer.he} will remember it.
choices.give_back_the_coin: Send back what {buyer.he} paid, and more, and be done with {buyer.him}.
choices.show_them_the_door: Tell {buyer.him} the bargain was for one vote.

texts.title: The Vote Still Undecided
texts.body: Your motion comes to the vote at the end of the session, and {doubter.name} of {doubter.house} has not said which way {doubter.his} house will go. {doubter.He} leans neither for it nor against. In a close count that is the vote that decides it. A head who thinks well enough of you leans your way, and {doubter.first} is not far off it.

choices.make_your_case: Go and make your case to {doubter.him} in person (1 influence). It may be enough to bring {doubter.him} over.
choices.have_them_to_dinner: Have {doubter.him} to dinner, and talk of anything but the motion (400 credits). It is the likeliest to bring {doubter.him} over.
choices.speak_from_the_floor: Speak for it from the floor, and let {doubter.him} hear it there. It may bring {doubter.him} over, if {doubter.he} was nearly there.
choices.leave_them_be: Leave {doubter.him} to make up {doubter.his} own mind.

texts.title: The Empty Seat on the Bench
texts.body: When the vote was called, your house did not vote. {leader.name} of {leader.house}, who leads your bench, voted, and looked along the bench to see who had not. A house that sits on a bench and will not stand up with it is talked about on the bench before it is talked about anywhere else.

choices.it_was_conscience: Say you could not vote for it, and would not vote against your friends.
choices.say_it_will_not_happen_again: Say it will not happen again.
choices.send_a_gift: Send a gift to {leader.his} house, and no letter with it.
choices.your_vote_is_your_own: Say your vote is your own to cast or keep.

texts.title: A Feast for the Ayes
texts.body: Your motion carried. The houses that carried it expect to be thanked, and in the Reach that is done at a table. {ally.name} of {ally.house}, who voted with you, has asked whose table it will be.

choices.your_table: Give the dinner yourself, and seat {ally.name} at your right hand.
choices.their_table: Let {ally.first} give it, and go as {ally.his} guest. The city will say it was {ally.his} motion.
choices.a_letter: Thank them by letter, and keep your evening for yourself.

texts.title: The House That Voted Against You
texts.body: Your motion carried, and {loser.name} of {loser.house} voted against it to the end. {loser.He} has lost in front of the whole chamber, and {loser.house} remembers who it lost to.

choices.offer_them_something: Go to {loser.him} and offer {loser.him} something for {loser.his} trouble.
choices.let_them_lose: Let {loser.him} lose. It is what a vote is.

texts.title: An Old Grudge Moves a Motion
texts.body: There is a motion before the Senate against your house, and it is {rival.name} of {rival.house} who moved it. Nobody in the chamber is surprised. {rival.He} has held a grudge against your house since the chamber last saw {rival.him} come off worse against you, and {rival.he} has been waiting.

choices.answer_them_on_the_floor: Answer {rival.him} on the floor, and name the old quarrel.
choices.make_your_peace: Go to {rival.him} and make your peace. It will not stop this vote.

texts.title: An Old Grudge Against Your Motion
texts.body: Your motion comes to the vote this session, and {rival.name} of {rival.house} is speaking against it in every corridor of the Senate. It is not the motion {rival.he} minds. {rival.He} has held a grudge against your house since the chamber last saw {rival.him} come off worse against you, and this is the first chance {rival.he} has had to make you pay for it. A head who thinks ill enough of you leans against what you move, and {rival.first} does.

choices.buy_them_off: Send {rival.him} something to let it go (600 credits). {rival.He} may think well enough of you again not to lean against it.
choices.answer_them_on_the_floor: Answer {rival.him} on the floor, and name the old quarrel. {rival.He} will still lean against it; the chamber will think the better of you.
choices.let_it_cost_you: Let {rival.him} talk. {rival.His} house leans against your motion, and the grudge is spent on it.

texts.title: The Senate's Act Falls on a Friend
texts.body: An Act of the Senate has carried, against the votes of {friend.house}. {friend.name} fought it to the last, and has written to you: not to complain, {friend.he} says, but because a friend should hear it from {friend.him} first. {friend.He} would like to know what you mean to do. An Act is undone as it was made: by another Act, moved in the Senate.

choices.promise_the_repeal: Promise to move its repeal when the chamber will hear it.
choices.help_them_through: Send {friend.him} help to carry it through the year, and ask nothing.
choices.the_law_is_the_law: Tell {friend.him} the law is the law, for your house as for {friend.hers}.

texts.title: A Purse on the Senate Floor
texts.body: On the floor today it came out that you paid {bought.house} for its vote. The vote is struck, and the chamber thinks the less of your house. {bought.name} is the one who had to walk out past everyone, and is waiting to hear what you will say.

choices.take_it_on_yourself: Say before the chamber that it was your doing, not {bought.hers}.
choices.make_it_good: Pay {bought.him} for what it has cost {bought.him}.

texts.title: One of Yours Stands for Office
texts.body: {kin.Rel}, {kin.first}, has put {kin.his} name down for office at the coming count. {kin.He} has not asked your leave, and does not need it: it is {kin.his} name. The house can speak for {kin.him} at the count, or pay for a canvass, as it can for anyone of the house who stands. What {kin.he} has come to ask is what you will do yourself.

choices.walk_the_wards: Walk the wards with {kin.him}, so the city sees the house behind {kin.him}.
choices.teach_them_the_floor: Teach {kin.him} how a crowd is won.
choices.let_them_win_it: Tell {kin.him} an office is won by the one who stands.

texts.title: A Smear After the Election
texts.body: {accuser.name} of {accuser.house} lost at the count to one of your house, and is saying in every square that the count was bought. It was not, or not more than any count is. But it is being said, and the squares like to hear it.

choices.open_the_accounts: Open the house's accounts to the praetors.
choices.answer_in_kind: Pay a pamphleteer to say what is known of {accuser.his} own canvass.

texts.title: The Pamphlet Scandal
texts.body: Your pamphleteer and the one {accuser.name} of {accuser.house} pays have been at it all year. The squares have enjoyed it. Nobody believes either side, which is to say that both houses are now believed to have bought what votes they could. {accuser.first} has sent word that {accuser.he} will stop if you will.

choices.call_off_your_writer: Call off your writer. The squares will say your house blinked first.
choices.before_a_praetor: Have {accuser.his} pamphlets brought before a praetor.
choices.let_the_writers_write: Let the writers write. {accuser.house} will come out of it no better than yours.

texts.title: The One Who Won the Office
texts.body: {victor.name} of {victor.house} took the office {kin.rel}, {kin.first}, stood for. The count is posted on the Senate doors. {kin.first} wants to know whether the house will ask for it to be read again, and so do your people.

choices.congratulate_them: Go and congratulate {victor.him} where the city can see. {kin.first} will see it too.
choices.demand_a_recount: Demand the count be read again. {kin.first} will know the house fought for {kin.him}, and the squares will doubt the count.

texts.title: A Riot on the Day of the Count
texts.body: The squares do not believe the magistrates this year, and they did not believe the count. By noon there were stones at the booths and a crowd at the Senate doors, and the lictors have sent to every house to ask what it will do.

choices.keep_the_peace: Send your house's people to keep the peace at the booths. The commons will see who came.
choices.speak_from_the_steps: Speak to the crowd from the Senate steps. The squares may believe the count again.
choices.call_the_lictors: Tell the lictors to clear the squares. The magistrates will thank you; the commons will not.
choices.bar_the_doors: Bar your doors until it is over. The commons will see whose doors were shut.

texts.title: The Consul-Elect's Feast
texts.body: The count is done, and {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} is Senior Consul for ten years: {grandee.he} will preside, speak from the chair, break a tied Senate, and once in {grandee.his} term strike a motion with a veto. Tonight {grandee.he} dines the Senate. Everyone who means to have anything of the consuls in those ten years will be at that table, and everyone will see who is not.

choices.go_and_be_seen: Go, and be seen to go. A consul remembers who came to {grandee.his} table.
choices.send_a_gift_ahead: Send a gift ahead of you that the table will talk about. A consul remembers who came to {grandee.his} table.
choices.ask_for_your_bench: Go, and ask across the table what the consulship will do for your bench. It will not be liked.

texts.title: Your Colleague, the Consul
texts.body: You and {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} hold the two chairs of the consulship. Each of you can strike the other's business with a veto: once in the term, {grandee.first} will strike the first motion of yours that strikes at {grandee.his} house, at {grandee.his} bench's leader or at {grandee.his} bench's line, and the chamber is waiting to see which of you will try it first. {grandee.He} has asked to see you before the first session.

choices.divide_the_year: Divide the consulship's business between you: neither of you strikes the other's.
choices.keep_your_counsel: Keep your own counsel, and watch {grandee.him}. You will learn how {grandee.he} works.
